digest.component_or_area: rebar store compaction and branch history garbage collection
propositions: The tickets branch blobless CI checkout pack is 481 MiB against a 100 MiB budget; git gc/repack cannot shrink it because trees dominate the reachable object composition (95% of bytes) from 235K commits and 408K trees, with 69% of commits being derived enrichment/digest churn re-emitting a 270 KB root tree

Retired event tombstones are blobs but the guarded pack is blobless (zero blobs), so removing .retired files alone shrinks the pack by ~0; the only lever is collapsing per-event commit/tree history below a reclamation horizon into SNAPSHOT-anchored checkpoints

Under a remote-anchored N-day horizon combined with stale-clone forced override on reconnect, a .retired tombstone is provably safe to reclaim only if its folding SNAPSHOT is reachable from the sync remote ≥N days, the stale-clone override prevents resurrection by forced reset, and authorship_ledger position keys remain stable while commit_sha and enforce_since are re-anchored to the baseline

At the maximum safe horizon N=30d the commit/tree coalescing yields ~365–380 MiB (24% off the 481 MiB); achieving ≤100 MiB would require an unsafe <4-day horizon; therefore a temporary budget-raise bridge (W3) is unavoidable paired with structural fixes W1 (write-batching) and W2 (root-tree sharding)

On S3 git-remote-s3 backends the auto-doctor's never-discard-a-head invariant would resurrect a normally-pushed rewritten baseline by merging it back, so the publish-swap must acquire the per-ref push-lock, assert the head set is unchanged, back up bundles, write one rewritten bundle, delete originals, and bypass the auto-doctor

The original .retired-only GC scope cannot move the pack-shrink gate because it is symptomatic rather than addressing the root cause (write→commit amplification at ~14K commits/day with 69% derived churn); the effective lever is commit/tree collapse rewrite using core-git fast-import (portable, no third-party vendoring) followed by per-backend publish-swap adapters (git ref CAS via force-with-lease for standard remotes, exclusive S3 bundle replacement)
